code.why: The host process around the fetch is outside the in-process Worlds measured by life-coverage (architecture, Coverage). Conformance separately runs this serve factory and its HTTP inspect listener; the blind application walk drives its raw TCP listener.

The TCP stream's guard (src/stream.ts) for the World's own fetch failing a command: a non-ok answer, a malformed WireAnswer or a throw closes the connection with RFC 5321 4.2.3's 451 instead of leaving the client waiting. A World whose engine answers every command never draws it.

state.item: refusal Session.stage: MAIL helo|ehlo → mail from fresh
state.why: A command out of RFC 5321's order (4.1.4: MAIL after the greeting and outside a transaction, then RCPT, then DATA): nodemailer, every demanded application's client, sends them in order, as does Wout's monitor; only a client not speaking the protocol draws the 503.

state.item: refusal Session.stage: AUTH ehlo → (stays) from fresh
state.why: AUTH outside an EHLO session that has not begun a transaction: RFC 4954 lets AUTH follow only EHLO, before MAIL, which nodemailer, every demanded application's client, keeps; a client breaking that order is a peer not speaking the protocol.

AUTH sent again on a session already authenticated: RFC 4954 has the server refuse a second AUTH (503), which only a client that does not track its own session sends; nodemailer, every demanded application's client, authenticates once.
